meeting: Post Quantum Transaction Signatures (PQTS) Breakout #18 - November 11, 2026

sphincs_parameters.highlight: Lean SPHINCS lifetime debate still open: 2^30 (Antonio, who would accept starting at 2^24) vs. 2^24 (Matteo Vena / Project 11); Emile stated no strong opinion this call. Antonio: 2^24 = ~16M signatures, enough, but small enough that he doesn't want the anxiety of counting
Matteo warns larger lifetime hurts performance on constrained hardware (MPC, hardware signers); benchmarks and alternative solutions to be published in the coming days or next week
Daisugi testnet live with an intermediate Lean SPHINCS parameter set chosen by Project 11; next deployment will use the sphincs.art parameters agreed 2 weeks ago

falcon_research.highlight: Amit presented fixed-point Falcon on Cortex-M4: eliminates floating-point dependency, only 2-bit security loss, ~9.1M cycles for Falcon-512 and ~19.3M for Falcon-1024 (2x Dilithium gap, down from 4x)
Paper submitted to CHES 2027 in mid-October; not yet peer-reviewed; preprint at https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2431

Group reaffirmed: Ethereum L1 committed to hash-based signatures; Falcon tracked for ecosystem awareness (L2s, account abstraction). Emile noted EIP-8288 would allow Falcon on L1 in future; Solana has committed to Falcon

action_items.action: Coordinate with EthPandaOps to expand Daisugi testnet and deploy sphincs.art parameters with traffic generation
Publish benchmarks and alternative solutions for Lean SPHINCS parameter set trade-offs

decisions.decision: No final decision on Lean SPHINCS lifetime parameter; both 2^24 and 2^30 remain under consideration pending benchmarks
Ethereum L1 PQTS remains committed to hash-based signatures; Falcon tracked for ecosystem awareness only

targets.target: Daisugi expanded testnet with sphincs.art parameters — ~2 weeks (next call)
